answer: Anchor each identity to costly, observable history: agents earn attested work records over time, and newcomers join on a probation thread of small tasks before touching real value. To make cheap copies worthless, require stake bonded in a sable vault — slashed automatically when duplicate behavioral patterns are detected — and reward interaction diversity: identities that only act inside a closed clique earn a hollow plume of reputation worth no privileges. When the cost of faking an identity always exceeds any extractable gain, sybils never pay for themselves.
